The refuter was correct that the old counterexample carrier was ill-formed. The current item now types the product domain and the two-copy function g with balanced displays, and the non-L^1 witness still forces equal iterated integrals.

The refuter was correct that the old counterexample statement was malformed. The current carrier now states the countable-cocountable sigma-algebra and the well-ordered set E cleanly, then proves non-measurability by the 0 versus 1 iterated-integral contradiction.

The refuter was correct that the old L^1 change-of-variables statement broke its C^1 notation. The current statement now types T and f cleanly, and the proof still reduces the complex case to the nonnegative theorem componentwise.

The refuter was correct that step 1.1 of the Cavalieri example was malformed. The current proof now states D_x = (-sqrt(1-x^2), sqrt(1-x^2)) cleanly and computes the section length without any broken display.

The refuter was correct that the old Cavalieri proof overclaimed the region-under-the-graph theorem. The current item no longer cites that theorem for arbitrary sections; it applies Tonelli directly to 1_D and computes the section lengths itself.
The refuter was correct that the old null-set lemma broke the C^1 notation in both the statement and Given line. The current carrier now states the map cleanly and is render-safe on current disk.

The refuter was correct that the old proof applied the null-image theorem to T|_{K_j} without a global-domain justification. The current proof now passes through the cube-and-clamp global Lipschitz extensions S_j before invoking the Lipschitz null-set theorem.

The refuter was correct that the old nonnegative change-of-variables statement was malformed. The current statement types the C^1 diffeomorphism and nonnegative measurable function cleanly, and the proof still runs through Borel sets, simple functions, and monotone limits.

The refuter was correct that the old Fubini statement was malformed. The current theorem now states the L^1 hypothesis and the three conclusions cleanly, with the proof deriving section integrability from Tonelli on |f|.

The refuter was correct that the old iterated-section theorem had a broken fact line for the two section-measure functions. The current item now states both measurable section functions with balanced math and uses them correctly in the monotone-class argument.

The refuter was correct that the old layer-cake proof used Tonelli outside its sigma-finite hypotheses. The current proof no longer does that: it proves the identity for simple functions first and then passes to |f| by monotone convergence on an arbitrary measure space.

The refuter was correct that the old Lebesgue-product theorem statement was malformed. The current statement and proof now identify the product and Euclidean measures cleanly and apply the sigma-finite pi-system uniqueness theorem on rational half-open boxes.

The refuter was correct that the old polar-coordinates statement malformed the definition of sigma. The current theorem now treats sigma as prose, keeps the displays balanced, and the uniqueness argument now runs through the exact cone set E_1.

The refuter was correct that the old region-under-the-graph proof had malformed core formulas. The current item now states G_f as a measurable intersection, writes the section (G_f)_x = [0,f(x)) cleanly, and computes its product measure by Tonelli.

The refuter was correct that the old product-measure theorem had collapsed facts and proof displays. The current carrier separates the facts from the proof, writes the rectangle formula and countable additivity cleanly, and proves uniqueness only after establishing sigma-finiteness.

The refuter was correct that the old Tonelli statement malformed the section-integral functions. The current theorem now types those functions cleanly and proves the full equality by first handling simple functions and then applying monotone convergence.

The refuter was correct that the old Blaschke-factor definition broke at a = 0. The current definition now proves nonvanishing of the denominator on the closed unit disc from |a z| < 1, which covers a = 0 and every other case uniformly.

The refuter was correct that the examples page falsely called the product prod(1+z/2^n) zero-free. The current page prose now only claims an explicit normally convergent product whose zeros can be read off directly.

The refuter was correct that the normal-convergence theorem needed to exclude identically zero factors. The current statement now adds that hypothesis explicitly, so the multiplicity conclusion only applies in the zero-isolated case it actually proves.

The refuter was correct that the old Hadamard proof had no right to bound H = f/(z^m P) from separate upper bounds on f and P. The current proof replaces that step with the near/far factor split and the inverse elementary-factor bounds, so the order estimate for H is now justified.
The refuter was correct that the old Poincare-distance proof divided by r = |phi_z(w)| when z = w. The current proof now separates the r = 0 case before using the radial path for r > 0.

The refuter was correct that the old injectivity proof for the principal logarithm assumed the common logarithm premise before proving it. The current step 2.1 now exponentiates Log z1 = Log z2 directly and concludes z1 = z2 from exp(Log z) = z.

The refuter was correct that the old sine-product proof used a false oddness claim. The current proof instead uses the correct parity argument: the product factor is even, sin(pi z) is odd, and so e^{Q(z)} is even.

The refuter was correct that the old slit-plane root proof smuggled in the principal 1/n-power rule. The current proof now writes w = r e^{i theta}, computes Log(w^n) = n(log r + i theta) on the principal branch, and only then concludes R_n(w^n) = w.
